DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

The combination of upper motor neuron signs (burning pain, weakness) and lower motor neuron signs (absent reflexes, fasciculations) in a patient with a year-long progressive course is highly specific for ALS. The mention of paresthesias is a common patient-reported symptom in early stages, despite the lack of true sensory loss in the disease pathology.
